policy.analysis_attachments_review: Complete-source semantic execution-safety review accepts the two raw-byte-hash-bound attachment modules and independently reviewed unchanged check_test_safety.py/run_safe_tests.py for analysis-attachments only. Exactly 31 explicit IDs (10 preparation, 10 import-owner, 4 reader, 7 qualification) retain one local helper dependency plus both bootstrap files and stdlib imports, with no Host/SDK import. Attachment filesystem operations and SDK-shaped RPCs are fakes; no tempfile fixture or real importer thread runs. Owner tests inject AsyncMock importers with controlled futures; the default asyncio.to_thread branch receives a cleanup-managed AsyncMock, never the real executor. Real stdlib effects are event-loop resources, tasks, futures, timers and cancellation. Eighteen exact AST callsite exceptions (10 helper, 8 test) replace the previous 14 records, including three moved _prepare_validated scopes and four narrowly reviewed new fixture calls; no forbidden execution is exempted. Checker execution only reads source/manifest and parses AST/JSON without importing tests/helper. Future separately authorized runner execution creates an owned base-Python worker, reader thread, fresh profile/evidence directories and retained logs; source review is not test execution, OS sandboxing, descendant confinement or unchanged-profile proof. No full-inventory, production filesystem/threading, SDK/Host integration, live, build or other-profile qualification. Changed helper/test/bootstrap bytes require affected semantic review and hash refresh before execution; Host-only edits outside this closure do not expand this review.
policy.default_selection: profile=None is full audit; named profiles select exactly their tests after validating the complete manifest schema
policy.non_exempt: forbidden_execution, shell_execution, inline_command, powershell_complex, powershell_unresolved and parse_error cannot be approved. An exception with any forbidden kind rejects the manifest globally, even outside inventory. Only the dedicated fixed_python_bootstrap shape can be reviewed for Python -c; compilation and dynamic imports require exact callsite review, never automatic approval.
policy.hash_contract: Lowercase SHA256 of complete raw file bytes, not generated source; null is pending, never approval. Source is exact AST call segment, or exact PowerShell line. Scope is dotted Python class/function nesting; PowerShell uses <file>.
policy.integration: Run gate before importing any test. Any diagnostic blocks all selection. Do not use unittest discovery to override returned paths. Imports/dependencies and selected files must remain unchanged between review, gate and runner.
policy.limitations: Initial inventory deliberately incomplete. Dependency closure is explicit, not an automated import graph. Python basic aliases only; unknown wrappers, monkeypatches and interprocedural flow still need human review. PowerShell is coarse positive command identification, not a parser: ordinary structure/interpolation and simple variable call targets require exact line review; constructed targets and unparsed quoting/subexpressions are non-exempt. Optional CJS is manual whole-source review. Frontend exceptions are pending handoff records, not scanner coverage.
policy.roles: test is runnable only for pure_mock/process classes; dependency/data/bootstrap use class support and are never selected. Dependencies are scanned and raw-byte hash-bound. Data is hash-bound only and cannot use a recognized source extension.
policy.bootstrap_trust_boundary: Only scripts/check_test_safety.py and scripts/run_safe_tests.py may use role bootstrap, review_kind bootstrap. They require separately reviewed full-file SHA256 and purpose, and are NOT scanned recursively or proven safe by this checker. The parent must review/import its bootstrap independently and bind manifest plus all closure bytes across gate/run; lstat checks are not atomic against concurrent mutation.
policy.runner_interface: check_repository(root, profile=None, process_tests=False, include_maintenance=False) returns (diagnostics, selected_test_paths), empty selection on any diagnostic. resolve_profile(manifest, name) is pure global schema validation returning copied tests/dependencies/test_ids lists; load_execution_profile(root, name) reads the validated manifest and returns the same metadata, NOT execution approval. Gate first, then bind the same snapshot; test_ids absent means all tests in the explicit files, present means exact module.Class.test_method IDs statically present in those modules. No discovery fallback.

Remaining inventory reviews are pending. Shared bootstrap hashes do not approve pii-core. No global inventory or process-test qualification is supplied. installer-success is intentionally absent until separately qualified.

Future authorized runner execution creates one owned base-Python worker, a reader thread, fresh profile/evidence directories and retained logs; not an OS sandbox, descendant confinement or unchanged-profile proof. The two new inventory records bind the filesystem-only test/helper review; no test execution, real ACL/symlink qualification, Host/SDK integration or other profile approval is supplied.
policy.analyze_progress_review: Complete-source static review accepts the two inventory-hash-bound progress modules and independently reviewed unchanged scripts/check_test_safety.py and scripts/run_safe_tests.py for analyze-progress only. Exactly 25 IDs use in-memory synthetic events, mock subscriptions/sinks/ownership and injected clocks, with some default time.monotonic reads; no Host/SDK import or process/network/registry/file mutation in these fixtures. Scanner reports 43 occurrences represented by 39 exact path/scope/kind/source exceptions (identical occurrences share one schema key); no forbidden kind is exempted. Checker inspection is read-only and imports no selected tests/helper. Runner source review covers future separately authorized owned worker/thread and fresh profile/evidence writes, not an OS sandbox, descendant confinement or unchanged-profile proof. No tests, live checks, builds or Host integration were executed or qualified. Changed module bytes require affected review and hash refresh by the coordinating review, not automatic reapproval.

inventory.purpose: Complete-source execution-safety review: 31 explicit IDs (10 preparation, 10 import-owner, 4 reader, 7 qualification), stdlib and analysis_attachments only; no Host/SDK import. Preparation uses in-memory readers or empty inventories. ReaderTests mocks os.lstat/open/fdopen/fstat/close and stream access with cleanup-managed patches and synthetic stat records. No real attachment filesystem, tempfile, process, registry or service access. Qualification uses AsyncMock RPCs and synthetic models; base64 roundtrips are inert data. Owner asyncSetUp injects an AsyncMock awaiting a controlled future and patches shared asyncio.to_thread to fail if unexpectedly awaited. Only the default-path test replaces that mock failure with a fixed PreparedAttachments return, never executing its callable argument or a real thread. Timeout helpers patch wait with sleep(0) and synthetic pending sets. Other cases use real wait, task/callback/cancellation scheduling and one cancelled 0.01-second timer; teardown resolves the controlled future and gathers the retained task before cleanup restores patches. Late failures are synthetic and consumed without logging; payload mutations and bilingual notices are in-memory. Existing qualification timeouts use two 0.001-second waits. Real isolated-loop OS resources remain effects, not remote access. Eight exact AST fixture-call records cover four retained calls plus two create_future calls, one local Mock marker and one payload-list clear. Source review only; no tests or real filesystem/thread/SDK behavior qualified.

Complete-source execution-safety review: stdlib-only definitions, no import-time product I/O or Host/SDK import. validate_attachment_metadata lexically validates and freezes descriptors/counts; prepare_attachments delegates to _prepare_validated. UTF-8 text, inert base64 blobs and fixed bilingual notices stay in memory. Ten helper AST records retain exact sources, with three preparation scopes moved to _prepare_validated. read_download has real read-only filesystem APIs, intercepted by five os mocks and mock stream in ReaderTests; other fixtures use injected readers or empty inventories. AttachmentImportOwner validates before await, skips empty imports, owns one task, uses asyncio.wait with five-second caller budget, consumes late exceptions and returns fixed timeout/busy/failed snapshots. Its conditional default asyncio.to_thread(_prepare_validated, snapshot, read_download) is real production threading/I/O, but the sole default-path test replaces to_thread with AsyncMock; other owner paths inject AsyncMock importers and controlled futures. qualify_images invokes only synthetic AsyncMock RPCs in this profile and real or patched stdlib wait_for. _field uses vars on plain fixtures, not arbitrary-object getter protection. No staging, writes, logging or executable decoding. This source review does not authenticate callers or qualify Host wiring, SDK contracts, filesystem races, image safety or shutdown/cancellation of real OS reads.

Complete-source review for analyze-progress: 25 fixed unittest IDs import only stdlib and the reviewed analyze_progress helper. Synthetic SimpleNamespace/Poison events, list sinks, Mock subscriptions/unsubscribes, throwing mocks and local ownership callbacks exercise bounded projection, retry/deactivation, closed schema and budgets. Captured handlers invoke only AnalyzeProgress.listen.handle; no generated code. Clocks are injected constants/mocks or default monotonic reads. No Host/SDK import, file writes, process, network, registry, sleep or live subscription. Static review only; no tests executed or integration qualification.

Complete-source review for analyze-progress: stdlib-only bounded in-memory reducer with fixed ASCII alias regex and UUID parsing, monotonic clock, exact primitive allowlists, request/attempt ownership and best-effort callbacks. Tool stages require both service and tool_id before consuming sequence; the existing bad-input test covers missing fields and unchanged sequence without adding test IDs or scanner exceptions. Dynamic attribute reads are limited to event/session fields; no object stringification or logging of raw fields. This profile supplies synthetic events/session and mock or local list/clock/ownership callbacks, never a real SDK subscription or sink. No file/process/network/registry operations. Callable seams are not a sandbox and this review does not qualify production Host wiring.

Complete-source review for repository-instructions: ten explicit filesystem-only tests import the reviewed helper and stdlib, never Host/SDK. Real effects are TemporaryDirectory creation/cleanup, mkdir, synthetic byte writes/reads, lstat and unlink inside each fresh runner TEMP fixture. Scoped builtins.open and os.lstat patches simulate permission and selected-entry disappearance errors; no ACL changes, symlink creation, process, network or registry operations. original_open invokes the saved builtins.open on the fixture path in rb mode; spies assert the selected path and mode. Source review only, not executed tests or real broken-link qualification.

Complete-source review for repository-instructions: stdlib-only helper checks exactly Root/AGENTS.md then Root/.github/copilot-instructions.md with lstat, reads the selected entry bytes once and strictly decodes UTF-8. No Host/SDK imports, writes, discovery, process or network effects; source review does not qualify Host error mapping or session integration.
